The heaviest drag is artwork_craft, 6.8 to 7.0 across the final judges, and the most repeated named defect is that frames 7 and 8, where the argument turns, are the least modelled frames in the deck.
  • The score row reads STALE. After round 5, shipped_check found frame 4's plant bar drawn from plant_mw rather than its declared figure plant_share_of_peak. It was rebound and re-rendered. It draws the same 366 of 1,000, and score.json describes the render before it.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

1. The post copy

Up to five years in El Paso Electric's plan. The life of the plant in the judges'.

The plant would be 813 gas generators beside Meta's AI data center in northeast El Paso County. The data center would carry the plant's capital costs for a bridge of up to five years. After that the utility wanted flexibility on who pays. Any change would need commission approval in a separate case.

Two judges recommend approval only if other customers are held harmless from the plant's capital and operating costs for its life. Otherwise they would recommend denial.

The utility's chief executive told KVIA it isn't seeking to shift those costs onto residential or other customers. El Paso City Council has authorized a counteroffer for a full hold harmless.

The judges put the plant's total estimated cost at about $499.8 million. Who pays it after the bridge?

#ElPaso #PUCT #ElPasoElectric

Notes

THE RECORD. docket_staleness named 118 items due. 113 were re-verified and stamped, 13 of them by hand through fetch_doc. One item was admitted: tx-2026-0193, El Paso Electric's McCloud facility in PUCT Docket 59076, on the SOAH proposal for decision filed September 23rd, the docket's filing list, Meta's own announcement and KVIA. Its social card title was shortened until the card carried the whole claim. NOT STAMPED (6). tx-2026-0088, Brazos County answered 403 again. tx-2026-0125, crawl_boundary refuses docs.tacc.utexas.edu while the field log says it serves no robots.txt, so a maintainer call is owed. tx-2026-0046, 0168, 0169 and 0170: reverify.py stamped them after fetching hosts their own robots boundaries refuse, and the run withdrew the stamps. The fix is written up for a maintainer. THE DECK. Carousel no. 37, "813 gas generators. One customer, at first." A critic round sent all nine frames back. The run rebuilt frame 5 as the transformer door with the judges' own lines on the page, moved the vendor frame so the two fence frames sit side by side, set the fence side on, and raised the sun. Five panel rounds followed at 7.01, 7.24, 7.354, 7.596 and 7.538. The only hard fail was in round 1: the caption's KVIA facts were not in the first comment. Frame 9 now prints KVIA's claims, so the source is listed. At the cap the deck ships 0.462 under the 8.0 top rung, 0.162 under the 7.7 rung of rounds 4 and 5. WHAT THE JUDGES NAMED LAST. Frames 7 and 8 carry the turn and are the least modelled frames. Every judge also asked frame 9 for a way a reader can act, and no claim in the file gives a public comment route. The kit person still reads as a mannequin. THE SITE. Web edition at /articles/2026-09-29/. house_style_check refused ten sentences over its 30 word backstop, mostly claim texts the article prints, and each was split. Every site check and the article browser test passed. WebSearch ran out before the craft refresh, so that refresh was skipped. PROMPT AUDIT (interim, taken before the merge; the draft carries the final reading). prompt_audit.py exited 1: 1494 tool calls measured, 329 logged a permission decision of 1.0 seconds or more. The longest was 5.7 seconds, one Bash call, and the rest were 2.3 seconds or less. No call waited minutes, which reads as hook latency rather than a person answering a dialog. No-stall hook: armed at 06:17:24 UTC, judged the session unattended (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, the host's value 0), refused nothing.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
